articles.title: Chiefs fans could pay up to $50,000 extra after taxpayers contribute $1.8 billion to new stadium
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs fans have spent decades making Arrowhead Stadium one of the NFL's most recognisable home venues.
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs fans have spent decades making Arrowhead Stadium one of the NFL's most recognisable home venues. But the team's planned move to Kansas could bring an uncomfortable change to that relationship. Even after taxpayers agree to cover a major share of the new stadium's construction, supporters may have to pay thousands of dollars for the right to buy season tickets. The proposal has put owner Clark Hunt under scrutiny, raising questions about whether loyal fans could end up paying twice for a stadium they are already helping finance.Chiefs stadium deal puts personal seat licenses under the spotlightThe Chiefs are preparing to leave Arrowhead Stadium after nearly 50 years, with their new domed home in Wyandotte County, Kansas, expected to open in 2031. The project has an estimated stadium construction budget of $3 billion, with Kansas expected to cover up to 60% through public financing. The Hunt family and the franchise are responsible for the remaining 40%.However, the funding agreement has raised concerns because it allows the team to use personal seat licenses, commonly known as PSLs, to help meet its private financial commitment.A PSL does not include a match ticket. Instead, supporters pay an upfront fee for the right to purchase season tickets for a particular seat. They must still pay the regular ticket price every season.The bigger concern is where that money goes. Under the agreement, PSL revenue will count towards the team's 40% contribution to stadium construction. The proceeds will go to a construction account and reduce the amount the franchise needs to provide from its own resources.That means supporters could indirectly help cover part of the Hunt family's financial responsibility, despite public funds already covering most of the stadium cost.The potential expense is not small. When the Buffalo Bills introduced PSLs for their new stadium, prices ranged from $1,000 to $50,000 per seat. The Chiefs have not announced any prices or confirmed whether they will introduce the system.Clark Hunt addresses Chiefs fans' concerns over additional costsHunt has acknowledged that the franchise is considering the option, although he stressed that no final decision has been made.“We haven’t made a firm decision on that, but it’s definitely under consideration,” Hunt said, according to Sports Business Journal.His comments have done little to ease concerns among supporters who have enjoyed attending games at Arrowhead without paying separate seat licensing fees.Chiefs fan David Whitaker called the possibility a “scam” while speaking with FOX4. Longtime season-ticket holder Tom Randolph also questioned whether the additional expense would be worth it.“It’s definitely been on my mind as a big point of concern because we’ve already paid that barrier to entry seven years ago when we first bought tickets,” he said. “If it’s going to be anything over $2,500, it’s a tough sell for me.”With the stadium still several years away from opening, the Chiefs have time to settle the issue. But the debate has already exposed a growing frustration among supporters: they want a modern home for their team, not another financial hurdle standing between them and game day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady faces new business hurdle as Elon Musk’s lawyer joins $4.2 billion Chelsea investment talks
articles.summary: Chelsea could soon attract two high-profile names from very different worlds.
articles.body: Chelsea could soon attract two high-profile names from very different worlds. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady is reportedly exploring a move into the Premier League club, and he may not be the only new investor. Alex Spiro, the lawyer known for representing Elon Musk, is also seeking a stake through Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital. Their potential involvement points to a fresh phase in the club’s ownership story, as Clearlake looks for new financial partners following a major change in its shareholder structure.Tom Brady and Alex Spiro pursue minority stakes in ChelseaAccording to The Guardian, Brady and Spiro are in discussions to invest in Clearlake Capital, which controls Chelsea. If the deals go through, neither man would receive voting rights at the football club. Instead, they would become limited partners in the investment firm, giving them a financial interest without direct influence over Chelsea’s decisions.The proposed investments are expected to be much smaller than the existing ownership stakes. Clearlake is preparing to take full control of 86.5% of Chelsea after agreeing to buy out former partners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter for around £1 billion. The transaction was agreed in September and is expected to be completed by the end of 2026.Swiss philanthropist Hansjorg Wyss, another member of the previous ownership group, has chosen to remain involved by purchasing 12.9% of Clearlake’s shareholding. Any new investors are expected to follow a similar arrangement.Brady's interest in Chelsea comes shortly after he sold his 3.3% stake in Championship side Birmingham City. He joined the club's ownership group in August 2023 and later became chair of its advisory board. His involvement also featured in the Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & the Blues.The former NFL quarterback has maintained links with Clearlake's leadership, particularly Behdad Eghbali, who has played a key role in discussions. Brady also attended Chelsea's Club World Cup triumph in New Jersey last year.Who is Alex Spiro, Elon Musk’s lawyer eyeing Chelsea?Spiro brings a different kind of profile to the proposed investment. The New York-based attorney has represented Musk since 2018 and advised him during his $44 billion purchase of Twitter, now known as X, in 2022.His client list also includes celebrities such as Alec Baldwin, Kim Kardashian and Jay-Z. Spiro helped Baldwin secure an acquittal in 2024 after the actor faced involuntary manslaughter charges following the fatal shooting of cinematographer Halyna Hutchins on the set of Rust.He is also representing investor Joshua Kushner in a legal dispute involving Uefa and Fifa-related business plans. Kushner's company, Thrive Capital, was the lead investor in a reported $4.2 billion Fifa World Cup investment scheme.Chelsea have declined to comment on the proposed investments. For now, Brady and Spiro's involvement remains under discussion. However, their potential arrival would add two influential figures to Clearlake's growing investor network as the ownership group reshapes its position at Stamford Bridge.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has made it clear how much the 2026 NWSL Championship means to her and the city of Kansas City. The Kansas City Current co-owner is backing her team ahead of its title clash against the Washington Spirit, partly owned by NBA legend Magic Johnson. With the Current chasing their first NWSL championship and Washington looking to add another trophy to its collection, both ownership groups have plenty riding on the result. Mahomes shared an emotional message about the team and her connection to Kansas City ahead of Saturday’s final.Brittany Mahomes Explains Why the Kansas City Current’s NWSL Final MattersMahomes, who is married to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, spoke about her connection to the city and why the championship is an important occasion for the club. She has been part of the Current’s ownership group and has followed the team’s growth over the years.“This is huge for this organization and for Kansas City in general, and I’m just so proud to be a part of it, and I’m really excited for these girls,” Brittany Mahomes said. “Kansas City is our home. Patrick and I, you know, have been here for a while, and we really care about this city, and we care about this community, and I love soccer.”Her support comes as the Current prepare for their second appearance in the NWSL Championship. The club last reached the final in 2022 but lost 2-0 to the Portland Thorns. This time, Kansas City has another opportunity to win its first league title.The Current also have plenty of confidence heading into the game. They have won seven consecutive matches, including their 2-1 semifinal victory over Gotham FC on November 15. Haley Hopkins scored the winning goal in the 89th minute to send Kansas City into the championship game.Mahomes also made it clear that the players have the support of the entire city as they prepare for the biggest game of their season.“I believe in them with my whole heart,” Mahomes added. “I think the city believes in them. We’re all rallying behind you. To see this organization where it is today and for these women to be playing in the final is huge.”Magic Johnson Wants His 19th Championship Ring as Washington Spirit Face KC CurrentWhile Mahomes is hoping to see Kansas City lift its first trophy, Magic Johnson has his own reason to be excited about the championship. The former Los Angeles Lakers star is part of the Washington Spirit’s ownership group and is hoping to add another title to his collection.“I’m just proud to be one of the owners in the NWSL,” Earvin Magic Johnson said. “I’m a winner. I need my 19th championship ring. So if we win on Saturday, it’ll be number 19 for me. And so I’m crossing my fingers.”Washington reached the final after beating Utah Royals FC 2-1 in the semifinal on November 14. The Spirit came from behind to secure the victory at Audi Field, with Sofia Cantore and Clara Luvanga scoring for the team.The Spirit finished third in the regular-season standings with 55 points from 30 matches. Trinity Rodman has been one of their leading attacking players, finishing the season with 14 goals. CBS will broadcast the match, which will also be available on Paramount+.Washington leads the overall series against Kansas City 6-5-1. articles.body: Al Davis became the Raiders’ head coach in 1963 and took over as the franchise's principal owner in 1972. In 1984, after the Raiders won their third Super Bowl, Davis coined the team’s famous motto: "Just win, baby." Al Davis also had a stint as the Raiders general manager. He died in 2011. Al Davis, a Pro Football Hall of Famer and central figure in NFL history, is portrayed in the newly released "Madden" film. articles.title: Puka Nacua's Injury Return Timeline for Rams Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Knee Surgery
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua faces a recovery time of four to five months after undergoing MCL surgery, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua faces a recovery time of four to five months after undergoing MCL surgery, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Nacua will miss the remainder of the regular season as well as the playoffs before he's expected to make a healthy return for his 2027 campaign, per Schefter.

The two-time Pro Bowler was previously placed on injured reserve after suffering an MCL injury during Los Angeles' 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 9.

On Friday, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua underwent the MCL procedure on Tuesday and would miss "a couple months."

While a potential playoff return for the 25-year-old wasn't officially ruled out at the time, there was still pessimism surrounding his short-term outlook after surgery.

The Ringer and Netflix's Tom Pelissero reported earlier on Saturday that there was "virtually no chance" Nacua would be able to return in 2026.

Los Angeles' receiving corps has been hit hard by injuries this season, as Davante Adams currently remains on injured reserve after undergoing hamstring surgery .

The Rams entered their 2026 campaign with Super Bowl expectations following a busy offseason in which they acquired star pass-rusher Myles Garrett and star cornerback Trent McDuffie before Aaron Donald came out of retirement to return to his former team.

Los Angeles is currently tied with the Seattle Seahawks for the No. 2 in the NFC West standings at 6-4.

Nacua started his season on a high note prior to the injury, hauling in 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns across his first seven appearances.

articles.title: Cowboys Could Cut Ties With Injured All-Pro in $27 Million Decision
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys made a series of roster moves, including putting DaRon Bland on IR--and possibly ending his career with the team. The post Cowboys Could C...
articles.body:
It's not a major surprise to find that Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland has landed on the injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. The team had indicated it would be a multiple-week injury, and the Cowboys need all the roster spots they can muster. But for Bland, the injury could be something more significant–it could end his career as a Cowboy.

It would, of course, be a sad end for a player who made waves in 2023 when he earned an NFL All-Pro nod for intercepting nine passes and returning five for touchdowns. It was a brilliant season for Bland, who appeared to be developing into a star after five interceptions in 2022, his rookie year. Not bad for a fifth-round pick out of Fresno State. But then, Bland hurt his foot in 2024. The team was still confident enough in him to five him a four-year, $92 million extension, but that proved ill-advised. Bland was never quite the same after the foot injury.

Indeed, he has gone from 14 interceptions in two seasons to one in his three most recent seasons. This year, he was allowing quarterbacks a 120.1 rating when he was targeted and allowed receivers to catch 36 of the 57 passes thrown his way. Because the Cowboys have used so many injured reserve spots, the team might have to rule Bland out for the season–and then the work almost certainly begins on wiggling free of his contract.

Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star Telegram explained : "DaRon Bland's $12M base salary for 2027 becomes fully guaranteed on March 17. The Cowboys can cut him before then (after the start of new league year) and take on ~$21.5M of dead cap in 2027, or they can designate him as a post-June 1 release and spread the dead cap hits with ~$6.46M in 2027 and ~$15.1M in 2028."

Considering the Cowboys will be weighing how to keep new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on board–he will be a free agent in March–making Bland a post-June 1 looks like a near certainty.

articles.title: Sean McVay Explains Decision on Puka Nacua’s Potentially Season-Ending Surgery
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL after suffering a sprain against the Washington Commanders. The post Sean McVay...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed the reasoning behind wide receiver Puka Nacua's MCL surgery after suffering a sprain against the Washington Commanders.

Nacua is also dealing with a sprained PCL and turf toe as well as a three-game suspension for breaching the NFL's personal conduct policy. Earlier in the season he also dealt with a calf strain and a groin injury, causing him to miss a couple of games.

The Rams initially didn't want to place Nacua on injured reserve upon his injury due to the current state of their roster, but ultimately decided IR and surgery was the right decision.

"He and his agent wanted to get the full scope so that you can really have the appropriate amount of information and then be able to make the right decision," McVay said. "Then ultimately, that was what led to feeling like this was the best decision for him and for the long term in terms of his return to coming back."

With his surgery, Nacua is likely to miss the remainder of the NFL season, heavily affecting the rest of the Rams' year.

Nacua broke onto the scene in 2023, and has routinely been the Rams' best receiver since making his NFL debut that season.

Through seven games this year, Nacua had 70 catches and 715 yards, scoring four touchdowns in the air. He also rushed seven times for 41 yards and a touchdown.

His best game of the year came against the Commanders, when he caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown before suffering his injury on the Rams' final offensive snap of the game.

The Rams don't have many options behind Nacua either, as Davante Adams is also on injured reserve after rupturing his hamstring earlier in the season. Konata Mumpfield led the Rams in receiving in their last game with three catches and 81 yards, but most of the offense for the rest of the season will come on the ground via Blake Corum and Kyren Williams.

Los Angeles is tied for second in the NFC West with the Seattle Seahawks at the moment, and will remain there this week with both teams on bye. The Rams' next opportunity to pull away from Seattle comes Wednesday, when they face off against the Green Bay Packers at 5:00 p.m. PT.

Every week during the season, the NFL announces fines on Saturday for games played the week before. So, the league's Week 10 punishments are out. "The rules are intended to protect the players from unnecessary risk, promote player safety and emphasize sportsmanship and respect of teammates, opponents, coaches, officials and fans," the NFL notes on its official website .

As you can probably guess, Lamb was slapped with a fine this week for actions during the team's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

The NFL is fining Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb $23,882 for unnecessary roughness after he was flagged for using his helmet. The fine stems from a block on 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir during George Pickens' 39-yard touchdown reception. Although officials initially flagged the play before picking up the penalty, the NFL reviewed the footage and determined that Lamb violated its helmet-use rules.

That $23,882 figure is actually the biggest fine of the week, so it may be enough to convince Lamb to think twice before making that kind of play again.

articles.summary: TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Florida following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a rideshare driver.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Florida following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a rideshare driver.

Harrell was in his hometown of Tampa when the crash occurred Friday morning. The Titans said in a statement that he was continuing to receive care in the hospital and they were in constant communication with his family.

Tampa Police said in a statement that Harrell was a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento "when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion."

The driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and struck a second vehicle before colliding with a utility pole. Harrell was thrown forward, struck the windshield and lost consciousness, the statement said.

The driver had minor injuries and was treated at the scene, according to police. The driver of the second vehicle, a woman in her early 50s, was not hurt.

The 24-year-old Harrell has not played for the Titans this season. He injured his ACL during the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve.

The Titans asked for privacy for Harrell and his family and said they would "provide an update when appropriate."

Tennessee selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft out of Michigan. He finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles and had 25 last season. He had 4 1/2 sacks and a forced fumble in 2025.

Harrell's father, James, also played eight seasons in the NFL.
